entity_linking.note: News headline links, 5 per ticker, so per-ticker intervals are wide.

impact.method: market model on SPY over [-120,-20] trading days; CAR[0,+1]; ticker-day level; day 0 = first session at/after publication (16:00 ET rule)
impact.v2_status: TBD (Benzinga event study, time split train <= 2018 / validate 2019-2020)
impact.note: v1 raw score has no fitted parameters (weights set a priori).

impact_v2.protocol: Benzinga train <= 2018, valid 2019-2020-07 (early stopping only); test on the 2021-22 replay ticker-days (post burn-in main, full window secondary)
impact_v2.pre_registered_rule: adopt only if 95% CIs of rho(v2)-rho(|s|) and rho(v2)-rho(v1) are both > 0 on test
impact_v2.applied_rule: spec rule, revised after the first test was seen (D-039): adopt if v2 beats v1 (CI of rho(v2)-rho(v1) > 0) on validation and on test
impact_v2.scope: company mentions; market-wide items keep v1 (D-042)
impact_v2.test_note: v1 on the test set is recomputed from each mention's stored drivers.
limitations: survivorship: delisted Benzinga tickers have no yfinance prices and are excluded
Benzinga is single-publisher, so breadth is constant in training (no learned effect)
domain shift: Benzinga headlines (2009-2020) vs GDELT news + tweets (2021-22)

moduleB_validation.method: predicted = shocks of the highest-impact stress test fired on the event date for the mapped class; realised = same proxies, close before event -> +10 sessions. If no run fired on the date the episode is reported as missed; the latest same-class run of the preceding 7 days is shown as supplementary context only.
